speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. To begin evaluating your skin lesion and rule out any oncologic implications, can you describe the specific characteristics, such as its size, color, and any changes in shape or border?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

The patient's history of heavy smoking, non-healing ulcerated lesions on both the penis and finger, and failure of prior treatments for syphilis and eczema are highly suspicious for malignancy. Given the location and chronicity, I am requesting a biopsy of the penile lesion and the finger lesion to confirm the diagnosis.
